title: Kane
build: Mastertronic cassette, 1985 (Ultimate Tape Archive Kane.tap, SHA-256 d6c066a6cdc3380026ace9cd5ecd7c4af98cf90851fb48b3b23777b328c48093)

multiply's second number, left at 0
multiply's product, low byte
multiply's product, high byte

the BRK vector's high byte

the NMI vector's high byte

Six bytes, $0334-$0339, the picture's three addresses as show_picture moves them to where the picture lies: its screen colours ($0334), its colour-RAM nibbles ($0336), and the end of those nibbles ($0338)
the screen colours' high byte
The start of the picture's colour-RAM nibbles, which is also the end of its screen colours, low byte
the nibbles' start, high byte
The end of the picture's colour-RAM nibbles, low byte
the nibbles' end, high byte
Sprite shape 15 in VIC bank 0, $03C0-$03FF: made a solid bar by build_ride_screen for the bars under a ride's band
The bar's last eight lines, $03D8 on: left empty, so the bar is eight lines high

The text screen of the status lines (the raster split shows it below the picture). Its top rows are never shown, and the game keeps a flag there for each sprite shape, $0400 + the shape's number: $FF when it faces as drawn, toggled by flip_shape each time the shape is mirrored. A stage sets the first 28 to $FF, a ride all 256.

The character set of the text screen at $0400, which shows the status lines, the title's text and the hall of fame: ninety-six characters, $0800-$0AFF, in the order of the C64's lower-case set, a to z at $01-$1A, digits at $30-$39 and capitals at $41-$5A. Besides the letters it draws the peace token's four quarters ($1B-$1E), the arrow mark ($22), a solid block ($40) and small figures and faces for the bars ($23-$26, $2A, $2B)
Ride 1's obstacles, pairs of a step along the map buffer and an object number from ride_objects (0 for none), ended by $FF at $0B31; place_object lays each one in
Sixty-two bytes after ride 1's list that nothing reads, in the same form of step and object pairs: $FF then 0 for most, and a few objects between
The train's obstacles, pairs of a step and an object number in the same form, ended by $FF at $0BA3
Ninety-two bytes after the train's list that nothing reads: $AA and $FF fillers, then pairs that look like a picture's packed screen colours

The game's entry: the loader jumps here when the tape has loaded, and a reset comes here through the CBM80 vectors at $8000. Turns the sprites off, copies three sprite shapes from $4000-$40BF into the stack page at $0101-$01C0, where unpacking a picture never reaches them (build_ride_screen copies them back to $7300), makes the border black, sets stage to 4 (the title) and runs on into show_picture.

Shows the picture for the stage in stage ($907B) and starts that stage. Jumped to from everywhere a stage ends, so it resets the stack pointer to $DF. Points BRK at brk_handler, installs irq_idle on raster line $D8 with CIA 1's interrupts off, wipes the bank-1 screen, sprites and bitmap ($4400-$7FFF) and colour RAM (clear_bank1), looks the picture up in picture_table and relocates the three addresses in its header, then unpacks its screen colours to $4400 and its colour-RAM nibbles to $8010 (unpack_runs), spreads the nibbles over colour RAM, unpacks its bitmap to $6000 (unpack_bitmap) and the sprite shapes packed under the I/O area at $D000 to $4800-$5FFF (unpack_rle), and goes on to start_stage.
X = $DF, the stack pointer this routine sets at $0C5E
drawing_picture = $FF while the screen is wiped, which keeps irq_top from setting the background colour

A picture's entry in picture_table is its address less one. Byte +0 is not read; bytes +1 to +6 are three addresses, assembled as if the picture lay at $A000, which this loop moves to where it really is: the start of its screen colours, of its colour-RAM nibbles, and the end of those nibbles. The bitmap's packed stream starts at +8.
VIC bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF), bitmap mode, multicolour, screen $4400 and bitmap $6000, dark grey background
Each byte of the nibble buffer at $8010 makes two colour-RAM cells, the high nibble first, until colour RAM ends at $DBFF
The picture's sprite shapes: packed at $D000 under the I/O area, unpacked to $4800-$5FFF

Unpacks a picture's bitmap from the stream at (zpa_26) to (zpa_28), reading each byte with every ROM and the I/O area switched out, so the stream can lie under them. A byte other than $00, $55, $AA or $FF is copied as it is; one of those four is followed by a count, and is written that many times (a count of 0 means 256). Waits a little after every byte it writes (short_delay), so the picture appears as it is unpacked. Stops when the destination passes $7F3F, the end of the bitmap at $6000, or the source reaches the address in unpack_end ($90E8).

Unpacks a stream of pairs, a count then a value, from (zpa_26) to (zpa_28): writes the value count times (0 means 256) until the source reaches the address in unpack_end ($90E8). Used for a picture's screen colours and for its colour-RAM nibbles. If the destination ever reaches page $CF it jumps to the KERNAL's reset routine at $FCE2, which restarts the machine; a picture's destinations are $4400 and $8010, so this never happens with the game's own pictures.
Waits a few dozen cycles (seven turns of a loop), keeping A: the pause after each byte unpack_bitmap writes.

The vertical fine scroll the raster handlers give $D011 (its low three bits): 3 on the title and in a stage's status lines; on a ride 3, 2 or 0 by level, which lifts the whole ride screen a line or three
The obstacle band's horizontal fine scroll, 0 to 7, written to $D016 by irq_ride_4
The fine scroll of the train's rows, or of ride 1's hills, 0 to 7, written by irq_ride
Sprite 0's x, copied to $D000 by irq_bottom: the top of the archer or the Marshall; on a ride, the other half of the rider when he is thrown
Sprite 0's y: $AA for the standing figure; marshall_dies drops it as he falls
Sprite 1's x: the middle of the figure; the rider on a ride
Sprite 1's y: $B1 for the standing figure
Sprite 2's x: the bottom of the figure; the first of the horse's six sprites on a ride
Sprite 2's y: $BF for the standing figure
Sprite 3's x: the first duck, or the first gunman; the sprites from here on are indexed from it
Sprite 3's y: the first duck's height, or the first gunman's; a hit duck falls to $AE
Sprite 4's x: the second duck, or the second gunman
Sprite 4's y: the second duck's or the second gunman's
Sprite 5's x: the third duck, or the third gunman
Sprite 5's y: the third duck's or the third gunman's
Sprite 6's x: the arrow, which a hit duck carries eight pixels to its left; the fourth gunman
Sprite 6's y: the arrow, ten lines above a hit duck; the fourth gunman's
Sprite 7's x: the sight, where the arrow or the bullet goes
Sprite 7's y: the sight's
The eight sprites' ninth x bits, copied to $D010: a sprite past x 255 has its bit set
Which sprites show, copied to $D015

The second extra background colour, copied to $D023: 7 on a ride; $0E55, the third, is copied to $D024

The sprites' second shared multicolour, copied to $D026
Sprite 0's colour, copied to $D027
Sprite 1's colour, copied to $D028
Sprite 2's colour, copied to $D029; the sprites' colours from here on are indexed from it
Sprite 3's colour, copied to $D02A: a gunman turns white when he takes a place and when he is hit
Sprite 7's colour, copied to $D02E: the sight, flipped between black and white every frame by irq_bottom so it flickers
Sprite 0's shape, copied to $47F8 by irq_bottom ($43F8 on a ride)
Sprite 1's shape: the archer's arm takes $50 to $54 for the arrow's angle; on a ride the rider, $CA or $CB
Sprite 2's shape; on a ride the first of the horse's six (sprites 2 to 7)

Sprite 3's shape: the first duck's wings ($58-$5B), or in the shoot-out the first gunman's own shape, 1 ($4040), or a puff of dust ($4D-$4F); on a ride one of the horse's six shapes. The pointers from here on are indexed from it
Sprite 4's shape: the second duck's wings, or the second gunman's shape, 2 ($4080), or a puff of dust; on a ride one of the horse's shapes
Sprite 5's shape: the third duck's wings, or the third gunman's shape, 3 ($40C0), or a puff of dust; on a ride one of the horse's shapes
Sprite 6's shape: 1 ($4040) for the arrow, whose rows duck_loop rewrites for its angle; the fourth gunman's shape, 4 ($4100), or a puff of dust; on a ride one of the horse's shapes
Sprite 7's shape: 0 ($4000), the sight
Seventeen bytes, $0E69-$0E79, copied to $D000-$D010 by irq_ride_sprites: the eight wide bars under a ride's band, x $1F to $6F 48 pixels apart at y $A7, with the last three past x 255
Twenty-four bytes after the bars' positions that no instruction addresses, $FF then zeros
Four bytes, $0E92-$0E95: the rider's position (sprites 0 and 1, x and y) kept while he is thrown in a fall and put back after
Forty bytes after rider_saved that no instruction addresses, all 0
The ride's position in the map buffer, low byte ($0EBF high): the first of the forty columns copy_map_window shows; $8010 at ride 1's start, $81A0 at the train's
map_pos's high byte
The distance ridden, BCD hundredths of a mile, low byte; $0EC1 holds the miles. 0.01 a character

The ride's obstacles, nine of them, $0EC2-$0FA2: five rows of five characters each (25 bytes), object 1 first, laid into the map buffer by place_object
Ride 1's hills, four rows of fifteen characters, drawn twice across the top of the screen by build_ride_screen
Ride 1's clouds, two rows of seven characters, drawn above the hills
Where the rider sits when the horse faces left: x $AE ($0FED) and y $6A ($0FEE)
the rider's y facing left

the rider's y facing right, and after a jump

The last five bytes of jump_horse_y: $5F for the third top sprite and $74 for the bottom three
The horse's six sprites' positions facing left: x $93, $AB and $C3 at y $67 and at y $7C
The horse's six sprites' positions facing right: the same, with each row's x in the other order
The horse's frame, 0 to $1E, taken from the list for what it is doing; its six shapes start at horse_frame×6+16
Frames to ride 1's hills' next pixel of scroll: 4 less the horse's speed, so the hills move slower than the band
The horse's speed, -3 to 3, negative to the left, 0 standing; changed a step at a time by the stick
Frames to the next copy of the horse's shapes and positions to the VIC, from 4
Set every fourth frame by irq_ride_control, cleared by the ride's loop when it takes the horse's next frame
The shape being turned in set_horse_shapes, horse_frame×6+16 up
Frames before the stick can change the horse's speed again: 15 after a change, more when the train speeds up; a jump at speed 1 needs it below 9
Not 0 while the horse turns round, which plays the frames at $1065
Not 0 while the horse jumps, which plays the frames at $1056 with the heights at $0FF1
Set when the speed changes and cleared every frame by irq_ride_control; nothing reads it
The sprites that touched another sprite this frame, read from $D01E by irq_bottom: the arrow hitting a duck
Which of sprites 5, 6 and 7, the horse's legs, touch the band this frame, from $D01F by irq_ride_sprites
Not 0 while a fall is under way, so the collision test does not start another
Twelve bytes no instruction addresses: $FF, 0, then 5, 9, 14 up to 45, steps of four and a half
The rider's bob: flipped between 0 and $FF every second animation step; the rider's shape ($90EF) becomes $CB on a flip to $FF and $CA on a flip to 0
Steps to the next flip of $1036, from 2
The horse's frames while it stands, speed 0: $17, $18 and $19, three steps each, $FF to start again
The horse's frames at one or two steps of speed: 9 to $11, one step each
The horse's frames at full speed, three steps: 0 to 8, one step each
The horse's frames in a jump: $12 to $16, three steps each but the first, two
The horse's frames as it turns round: $1E down to $1A, three steps each
Two bytes after the frame lists that no instruction addresses: $28 and $14, 40 and 20
A credits line for the title's bottom row, forty screen codes: " DESIGN AND PROGRAMMING BY JOHN DARNELL "
The third credits line, forty screen codes: "A MASTERTRONIC PRESENTATION", centred
The train's carriages, five rows of twenty characters ($10C7-$112A), drawn twice across the top of the screen by build_ride_screen
The arrow's shape at nine angles, sixteen bytes each: eight rows of two bytes, which duck_loop copies into the bottom rows of sprite shape 1 ($4067-$407E)
The duck being moved, 2 down to 0
duck_index×2: the duck's x and y in the shadow registers, from spr3_x
The ducks' wing shapes, $58 to $5B, and $FF to start again
Where the three ducks start a stage: x $30 y $30, x $70 y $50, x 0 y $A0
The three ducks' places in wing_frames
Passes of the ducks' loop to the falling duck's next increase of fall_speed, from 3
Lines a hit duck drops each pass of the ducks' loop, 0 at the hit, one more every three passes
Passes of the ducks' loop a hit duck lies on the ground, from 5, before it is counted
The three ducks' state: 0 flying, $FF hit and falling
duck_falling for duck 1
duck_falling for duck 2

Sets up stage 1, the ducks in the canyon, and runs it: ends by jumping to duck_loop, whose RTS returns to start_play's caller and so to ride 1. Clears ducks_killed, ducks_home and tokens, sets ducks_per_token by level (3, 4 or 5), gives ten arrows (BCD $10), blanks the status lines, walks the archer in from the left edge (walk_right) until his sprites pass x 255 and stands him at x 257, places the three ducks from $11C2, turns on the archer, the ducks and the sight, writes the status text ($8FB9: "Birdies Killed" and "Birdies Home") and "Score", draws the ten arrows, starts the drum (effects bit 4), adds 10 points and puts the sight at x $A0, y $A0.
Forty-seven bytes after start_ducks that nothing runs or reads

The title picture's header: its entry in picture_table points here. Bytes 1 to 6 are the addresses of its screen colours, its colour-RAM nibbles and their end, assembled for $A000 and moved by show_picture ($1806, $18D0, $1946)

The title's bitmap, packed for unpack_bitmap ($00, $55, $AA and $FF followed by a count): the "Welcome to KANE" sign's upper half, character rows 0 to 11 and the first eleven cells of row 12, unpacked to $6000
The title's packed bitmap from row 12, column 11, to row 24: the rest of the sign and the black below it
The title's screen colours, packed for unpack_runs (pairs of a count and a value): the two colours of each 4 by 8 cell, unpacked to $4400
The title's colour-RAM colours, packed in pairs of a count and a byte that holds two cells' colours, the high nibble first: spread over $D800-$DBFF by show_picture
Ten bytes before duck_loop that nothing runs or reads

The ducks' loop, one pass every three to four frames (delay_count from $19, about 57,600 cycles; 3.7 frames a pass measured live): moves the ducks (move_ducks), reads the stick and moves the sight six pixels a step, from its start at x 160, y 160 to x 28-184 and y 46-160. With no arrow in the air it sets the archer's pose and the arrow's angle from the sight's position, and fire shoots: one arrow less, the arrow starts at x 255, y 170, and its step is the distance to the sight over 16 when the sight is 112 pixels or more to its left and over 8 when it is nearer, so an arrow shot at a sight high above the archer reaches it in half the passes and flies faster. The arrow's shape is drawn for its angle from the nine shapes at $112B, and the whistle sound starts. A shot whose upward step was 9 or more makes the next one wait ten passes (shot_wait). The stage ends when 39 ducks have got home or the arrows run out: with no token it is game over and the title; otherwise the archer walks off to the right, the bonus is tokens×3 lots of 99, counted onto the score, and duck_loop returns.

No arrow in the air: the angle. zpa_11 = (190 - sight y) × 16 over zpa_13 = (255 - sight x)/2 + 26 (divide); a quarter of the quotient, at most 8, is the arrow's frame, and half of it picks the archer's arm: $54 below 4, $52 below 6, $50 below 9, $51 above
The end test: 39 home (BCD), or no arrows left

Moves the arrow by its step, up and left (arrow_dx, arrow_dy), unless a hit duck is falling, when the arrow stays where it is. Once it is level with the sight or past it, it flies on until it leaves the top or left of the screen (y below 20 or x below 10); then it is taken away and the sight shows again, and a steep arrow (upward step 9 or more) sets shot_wait to 10.
Moves the three ducks (move_duck for duck 2, 1 and 0).

Moves duck duck_index (sprite 3, 4 or 5), once a pass of the ducks' loop. A duck that is flying and touches the arrow (the VIC's sprite collision bits, kept in collisions by irq_bottom) is hit: it plays the hit sample (play_hit) and scores 99 on level 1, 149 on level 2 and 198 on level 3. A hit duck falls faster and faster (fall_speed, one more every three passes) with the arrow stuck in it; when it reaches the ground (y 174) and five passes more, ducks_killed goes up by one (it stops at 30), the tokens become ducks_killed over ducks_per_token and the new token is drawn, an arrow is given back (up to ten), and the duck starts again from the left. A flying duck flaps its wings (the shapes at $11BD) and moves right by its speed; when it passes x 496, well off the right of the screen, ducks_home goes up by one and it starts again. A duck starts at x 0 at a height of 11×(5 to 15), not the height of another duck, with speed 2 on level 1, 2 or 3 on level 2 and 2 to 4 on level 3, all chosen from CIA 1's timer.
The hit duck has landed: the count, the tokens, the arrow back
The duck flies: the next wing shape from $11BD, the list ending with $FF
Off the right edge: one more duck home, drawn as a bar
The duck starts again: x 0, a speed, a height

Fifty-six bytes before draw_token that no code reaches: an unused routine that waits for the raster to wrap and then for two lines to pass ($1D96-$1DB4), and one that prints A as two digits at $0770 and $0771 ($1DB5-$1DCD)
Prints the BCD byte in A as two digits at $0770+Y and $0771+Y, row 22, the first left out when it is 0. Never called.

Draws peace token number tokens as a two-by-two block of characters $1B-$1E in yellow, with the carry set, at column 2×tokens+8 on row 23 ($07A1), or on row 22 ($0779) in a riding stage (in_ride set). With the carry clear it blanks the place after it instead, the token just lost.
Draws the arrows (or bullets) left as a row of the mark in arrow_char on row 21 from column 16, one for each of arrows (BCD), spaces for the rest of the ten, in purple.
Adds the BCD byte in A to pending ($8FA4-$8FA7), the points still to be counted onto the score. Returns with the zero flag from the top byte's add.

Draws a count as a bar: the BCD byte in A, as a number, is the count of cells filled with character bar_char in colour bar_colour, from (zpa_26) on the screen and (zpa_28) in colour RAM, bar_width cells to a row before it goes on in the next row.
The rest of move_duck: moves the duck right by its speed, setting its position bit past 255; a falling duck drops by fall_speed and carries the arrow ten lines above and eight pixels left of it

Blacks out the background and turns the sprites off, clears the bitmap from $7FFF down to $6000 a byte at a time with a pause after each, so the picture is wiped from the bottom up, with drawing_picture set, then clears colour RAM (clear_colours).
Waits until pending is 0: until the score has counted every point up.

Starts a riding stage, ride 1 (stage 1) or the train (stage 2), and runs it. Also the restart: F1 during a ride and a lost token come back here. Installs irq_idle, sets in_ride, blanks the screen and the sprites, clears the ride's counters, puts the ride at its start (map_pos $8010, distance 0.00 for ride 1; $81A0 and 4.00 for the train), starts the tune (the train has the train's sound instead: music_off and hoofbeats set), builds the screen (build_ride_screen, copy_map_window), writes "Score", installs irq_ride, sets the train's coach count by level (3, 7 or 11) and draws the tokens. The train gets its status text ($9043) and its sound's settings; ride 1 its two lines ($900B, $9027: "Time Remaining" and "Distance To Go"). Sets two minutes on the clock and adds 2 points, the A left from setting the minutes. Then runs the loop at ride_loop.
Raster handler that acknowledges the interrupt and returns: installed while a picture or a stage is set up.
The ride's set-up proper
flip_base $40: the ride's shapes are mirrored from $4000
CLI. The copy in copy_map_window names $2000 in its two instructions, which it writes over before they run, so the tracer took this address for a table

The ride's main loop. Nothing on its ordinary path waits, so it runs many times a frame (54 passes a frame on the train, measured live); the work done once a frame is in the raster handlers. Once the train is caught or 20 coaches ahead, every pass also clears the obstacles again (clear_obstacles), which slows a pass to about two and a half frames. F1 restarts the ride (start_ride) with no token lost and the clock and distance back at the start. For ride 1 it goes to ride1_step. For the train: the hoofbeats' volume rises as the coach count falls, the distance wraps from 0.00 back to 3.99 (the track loops: the train ride has no clock), as the hoofbeats' period ($9820) shortens the train speeds up (train_speed -1 at $13, -2 at $0E, and at $0B the horse's speed is set to -1, each with fifty frames before the stick works again), and when the coach count reaches 0 the train is caught: the obstacles are cleared, the engine is drawn in on the left from the columns at $8F5D, and the train slows until it stops. Then the bonus: 30, 50 or 70 lots of 99 by level, and tokens×5 lots of 99 three times; and the next level (ducks, stage 1, level up) or after level 3 the ending (stage 3), or the title when the ride was a practice.
The coach count is 0: the train is caught
The train has stopped: the bonus and the next stage
After the train: the next level's ducks (stage 1, level + 1), or after level 3 the ending (stage 3)

The train's ride, a pass of ride_loop. The track loops: at 4.00 miles the distance goes back to 0.01 (and at 0.00, in ride_loop, on to 3.99). When the coach count reaches 20 the obstacles are cleared, on every pass from then on, and $3B is set to the count, which stops the end of each scrolling train row being wrapped round; from 22, every ten passes (about 25 frames, as clear_obstacles slows each pass) the hoofbeats grow quieter and the horse slows a step, and fifty passes after it stands a token is lost (game over with none left, otherwise the ride starts again). Otherwise each time the count reaches a new low, 49, 74 or 75 points by level are added three times, and the count is shown on row 17.

Ride 1. At 4.00 miles the ride is won: the time bonus adds 15, 20 or 25 points by level (BCD) a number of times held in zpa_10. With a minute or more left that number is the clock's seconds, a BCD byte, plus $50 as a plain binary sum: 128 times at 1.30, 168 at 1.58. With under a minute left nothing sets it, and zpa_10 still holds the 0 that the end of unpack_rle or of a sample left there, so the loop runs 256 times, the biggest bonus. Then the shoot-out follows (stage 0). When the clock reaches 0.00 a token is lost: game over if it was the last, otherwise the ride starts again. Otherwise shows the distance to go, 4.00 less the distance, on row 17.

A fall (falls set by the collision test in irq_ride_sprites): the horse stops, one token less, the rider (sprite 1) is thrown in an arc in eight steps, the sample at $9E00 plays (play_whinny), and after thirty frame_delay waits, with no token left, it is game over. Otherwise the ride moves on three characters at a time the way the horse faced until the horse touches nothing. "F1 WILL RESTART LEVEL" then flashes on row 16
Game over from a ride: wipes the bank-1 screen (clear_bank1), turns the music back on and goes to the title.

The horse's animation, every fourth frame (counted by irq_ride_control): the rider's shape changes every other step, so he bobs in the saddle, and the horse's frames come from the list for what it is doing: standing ($1038), turning round ($1065), one or two steps of speed ($1042), three ($104C), or jumping ($1056, with the rider's heights at $0FF1)
Turns the six shapes of the horse's current frame (horse_frame×6+16 on) to face walk_dir (flip_shape where they do not) and sets them as its animation (set_horse_frames).
JMP ride_loop
Puts the horse facing right: its sprites' positions from $1011, the rider's two shapes ($CA, $CB) turned to face right, and the rider's place from $0FEF.
Puts the horse facing left: positions from $1005, the rider's shapes turned, and the rider's place from $0FED.
Waits for the ride's frame to end twice: until the IRQ vector is irq_ride and then is not, two times over.

Raster handler of the rides, line 1 (the top): VIC bank 1, multicolour text from the character set at $7800 with the screen at $4000, the train's fine scroll (train_scroll) and the screen's vertical scroll, the shadow sprite registers copied to the VIC with the pointers at $43F8, background blue, multicolours orange and brown (yellow on the train), sprites in front. On the train it swaps two of the character set's pieces every frame ($7BC8 and $7CE0, the wheels and the smoke); on ride 1 it counts the clock down a second every 50 frames and shows it on row 17 (zpa_48.zpa_47 minutes and seconds, BCD). Then counts the score (count_score) and plays the music (play_music). Next handler line $55.
Raster line $55: the multicolour bit set in $D016. Next handler line $6A.
Raster line $6A: the background orange. Next handler line $7D.
Raster line $7D: multicolours yellow and brown, and the obstacle band's fine scroll (band_scroll) in $D016. Next handler line $81.
Raster line $81: every sprite behind the background, and the sprite-to-background collisions cleared by reading them. Next handler line $9A.

Raster line $9A: reuses all eight sprites lower down the screen, doubled in width, as solid bars of shape 15 in the border's colour at the positions in $0E69. Checks the sprites' collisions with the background: when sprites 5, 6 or 7 have touched it, no fall is under way, and the fifteen characters at $4213 (row 13 from column 11) are all 0, it sets falls and freezes the horse's shapes. Next handler line $A8.
Raster line $A8: the text screen for the status lines (VIC bank 0, character set $0800, screen $0400, black). Next handler line $AF.

Raster line $AF: sprites off. Every fourth frame copies the horse's new shapes ($90EE) and positions ($91B6) to the shadow registers. Reads the stick: left and right change the horse's speed one step (from -3 to 3; 0 is standing) with fifteen frames between changes, and fire starts a jump while the horse is moving (at speed 1 either way, not in the six frames after a change of speed). Then scrolls the obstacle band by the speed, a character at a time moving map_pos and the distance (0.01 mile a character; ride 1 stops at 4.00 miles going right and at 0.00 going left), and on the train scrolls the train's rows by the difference of the horse's speed and the train's (train_speed), the coach count changing by one every twenty characters. Next handler irq_ride on line 1.
BIT $1EA5: hides the LDA $1E at $2CAF, where a train that is not stopping branches in to wrap the row's first character round; a stopping train puts a 0 there instead
Turns the BCD byte in A into two digit codes for the screen ($30-$39): the low digit's in A, the high digit's in X.

Draws the peace tokens on the status line, one icon for each token from 1 up to the count in tokens ($8FAC), by calling draw_token with the carry set for each. It always draws the first, so when tokens is 0 it draws one and leaves tokens at 1.

Builds the screen of a riding stage, ride 1 (stage 1) or the train (stage 2). Makes sprite shape 15 ($03C0 and $43C0, both VIC banks) a solid bar 24 pixels wide and 8 lines high, sets the shadow colours of $D021-$D023 to 8, 7 and 9, clears the map buffer, clears the screen at $4000-$42FF, colours the top five rows 1 (8 for the train) and the rest $0D, then lays the stage's objects into the map buffer from its placement list ($0B00 for ride 1, $0B70 for the train: pairs of a step to move along the buffer and an object number, 0 for none, $FF to end; place_object). Copies the ride's character set from under the KERNAL ($F6C0-$FEBF) to $7800, draws the scenery (the train's twenty-by-five carriages twice across, with a row of $77 below, or ride 1's hills and clouds), unpacks the ride's sprite shapes from $DA50 to $4400-$77FF, puts back the three shapes kept in the stack page at $7300, fills the first page of the text screen with $FF, and sets up the sprites: the horse's frames (set_horse_frames), positions from $1005, colours, sprite 1 multicolour, every sprite behind the background, and the falls count ($8FAD) to 0.
Ride 1's scenery: four rows of fifteen characters from $0FA3 at row 5 columns 0 and 25, then two rows of seven from $0FDF at row 3 columns 0 and 25
Both stages: the ride's sprite shapes and the three kept in the stack page, then the sprites' starting state

Copies ride object number A (from 1) out of the object table at $0EC2, 25 bytes each, as five rows of five characters into the map buffer at (zpa_26). The buffer's rows are 400 bytes apart, the length of the ride. Keeps zpa_26 and zpa_27.
Multiplies zpa_05 by zpa_06, both unsigned bytes: the product in zpa_07 (low byte) and zpa_08 (high byte). Leaves zpa_06 at 0.

Divides the 16-bit number in zpa_11 (low) and zpa_12 (high) by zpa_13 by subtracting it over and over: the quotient in zpa_14, the remainder in zpa_15 and in A. If the quotient passes 255 (a divisor of 0 does that) it runs on into show_timer_hex below instead of returning.

Prints the low byte of CIA 1's timer A as two hex digits (print_hex) at $0749 plus that same value, again and again until the low byte reads 0, then returns. Reached only by falling out of divide when the quotient passes 255; the aiming code's divisor is never 0, so it does not run in play.

Draws the ride's obstacle band: copies forty characters from each of the map buffer's five rows, starting at the ride's position in map_pos ($0EBE), to screen rows 10 to 14 ($4190-$425F). Keeps its source and destination in its own instructions: map_src at $3036 and band_dest at $3039.
The operand of the copy's LDA: the address in the map buffer of the row being copied, set from map_pos and moved on 400 bytes a row by copy_map_window
map_src's high byte
The operand of the copy's STA: the screen row being written, $4190 first, moved on forty bytes a row by copy_map_window
band_dest's high byte
Picks the six sprite shapes from A×6+16 on and stores them as two three-frame animations: shapes 0, 2 and 4 of the six in $90F0-$90F2 and shapes 1, 3 and 5 in $90F3-$90F5.

Unpacks a stream from (zpa_26) to (zpa_28), reading it with every ROM and the I/O area switched out, until the destination reaches the address in zpa_32 and zpa_33. A byte other than $00 or $FF is copied; $00 or $FF is followed by a count of how many times to write it. Unpacks a picture's sprite shapes ($D000) and a riding stage's ($DA50).
Clears the bank-1 screen, sprite shapes and bitmap ($4400-$7FFF) a byte at a time, waiting A turns of a loop after each byte, then runs on into clear_colours.
Sets every cell of colour RAM ($D800-$DBFF) to 0, black. The end of clear_bank1, also jumped to on its own.
Clears $8010-$880F, eight pages counted from $8010: the riding stages' map buffer, five rows of 400 bytes at $8010-$87DF, and the 48 bytes after it, up to the byte before gunman_step ($8810).

Sets to 0 every byte from 5 to $5D in $8000-$87FF, keeping 0 to 4 and $5E up: takes the obstacles out of the map buffer. It starts at $8000, below the buffer, so it also clears bytes of the CBM80 header there: the high bytes of the two vectors ($8001, $8003, both $0C), the "8" and "0" of the signature ($8007, $8008) and $800D. Until the next stage writes the header again, a reset finds no signature and starts BASIC, and the game is lost.
RTI: the NMI handler while the game runs, so the RESTORE key does nothing.

Runs after show_picture. Points BRK at brk_handler and NMI at nmi_ignore, writes the CBM80 signature with both vectors at $0C00 into $8000-$8008 (so a reset restarts the game), clears music_off and practice, sets the bitmap screen's $D011 value ($3B) and the text screen's fine scroll (3), and goes by stage: 3 is the ending, which follows here, 4 the title (title_screen) and anything else start_play.

The ending. Starts the tune, clears the status lines, draws the tokens left, installs irq_bottom, and slows the tune at the places listed at $8E5D (twice: see there); then plays the ending's sample at $FCC0 (play_ending_sample), shows the ending text a line at a time from $8CAC (irq_bottom scrolls it), waits for the last line, waits $C2 times frame_delay (about ten seconds), clears the bitmap and goes to the title.

The title (stage 4). Installs irq_title, checks the last score against the hall of fame and takes the player's initials if it is in (check_high_score), clears the score, writes the title text ($8EF0-$8F5C), sets stage to 1 and starts the tune (start_tune). Then waits: F1 opens the practice menu, fire on the joystick in port 2 starts a game at level 1, F7 shows the hall of fame until fire is pressed, and every so often the bottom line changes between three credits lines.
F7: the hall of fame, with "PRESS FIRE BUTTON" under it, until fire on port 2; then back to the title
The credits line on row 24 changes every 200 turns of the wait, in turn: the graphics credit at $3E3F (light blue), the line at $1077 (purple) and the line at $109F (light red)

F1 on the title. Asks "LEVEL 1 2 OR 3 ?" and waits for 1, 2 or 3 (level), shows the four stages and waits for F1 (the ducks: stage 1 through show_picture), F3 (ride 1: stage 1 straight into the ride), F5 (the shoot-out: stage 0 through show_picture) or F7 (the train: stage 2 straight into the ride). practice was set by the F1 that came here, and show_picture's start_stage clears it again, so only the two rides start with it set.

Raster handler of the title, line 1: VIC bank 1, multicolour bitmap at $6000 with the screen at $4400, black border and background; next handler irq_title_text on line $AB; then plays the tune (play_music).

Raster handler of the title, line $AB: VIC bank 0, text from the character set at $0800 with the screen at $0400, the text screen's fine scroll from text_scroll, sprites off; next handler irq_title on line 1.
Fire on the title: a new game at level 0 with the music off while show_picture draws the canyon

Starts the stage in stage after its picture is drawn (the shoot-out, 0, or the ducks, 1). Clears the shoot-out's counters and the sprite expansion, priority and multicolour, places and colours the Marshall's sprites from $9091, $90C4 and $90D5, empties the gunmen's table, clears the sound chip (clear_sid), installs irq_bottom, and for stage 1 goes to start_ducks. For the shoot-out it draws the tokens and the score, walks the Marshall in from the left, writes the status line ($8FE2), puts the sight in the middle, gives him six bullets and runs the shoot-out's loop below.

The shoot-out's loop, one pass every two to three frames (frame_delay; 2.8 frames a pass measured live): reads the stick, runs the gunmen (gunmen_appear, gunmen_aim, dust_puffs) and then moves the Marshall and his sight: up and down move the sight three lines at a time, between y $30 and the Marshall's y; left and right walk the Marshall, six pixels a step (three for the first step after he has stood still), and the sight follows his x (walking off the left edge needs bit 0 of $0E4F, his position past 255); fire shoots if he stands still and has a bullet
Fire: one bullet less, the gun raised for twelve passes of the loop (the shot is checked on the third, check_shot), the shot's sound

Checks the Marshall's shot against each gunman that is showing (the sixteen slots at $914D), using the gunman's position at $9169 and the size of his shape from $91CA: a hit when the sight ($0E4D, $0E4E) is inside the box. A hit turns the gunman's sprite white and, the first time, plays the hit sample (play_hit), adds one to bad_guys_killed, takes one from bad_guys_left, and gives (level+1)×2 lots of 99 points. The twelfth ($12 in BCD) ends the stage with a bonus, waits for it to be counted onto the score (wait_points) and goes to the train ride (stage 2). The bonus loop loads 5 into Y, which nothing uses, and repeats on a flag that the add leaves clear, so the bonus is 99 points for each level up to this one, (level+1)×99. The BRK at $379A would stop the game if a slot were not in the table at $9165.

Waits by counting a 16-bit loop down from $1400 (frame_delay_lo, frame_delay_hi): about 46,000 of the processor's cycles, which with the interrupts and the cycles the video chip takes is between two and a half and three frames. Entered at $380B with frame_delay_hi set first, a shorter or longer wait.
Counts frame_delay_lo and frame_delay_hi ($90A2, $90A3) down to zero: the wait itself, entered here with frame_delay_hi already set.
Writes A as two hexadecimal digits in yellow at $0749+Y and $074A+Y, the status line, keeping A.
Turns a value 0-15 in A into a screen code: $30-$39 for 0-9, and 1-6, the codes of A-F, for 10-15.
Puts the figure's three sprites ($0E40, $0E42, $0E44 their y positions $AA, $B1 and $BF) in their standing shapes $3F, $41 and $40, with black and white colours. Used by the archer and the Marshall.

Moves the figure's three sprites left by the step in walk_step (6, or the value set before the call), animating them (walk_animate); the sight (sprite 7) takes the same x. Clears a sprite's position bit in $0E4F, and the sight's, when it passes 0. Does nothing while sprite 0 is at the left edge (x below 16 with no position bit). Resets walk_step to 6.

Moves the figure's three sprites right by walk_step, animating them; the sight (sprite 7) takes the same x. Sets a sprite's position bit in $0E4F, and the sight's, when it passes 255. In the shoot-out, once the Marshall is past x 383, off the right edge of the screen, his bullets are put back to six, and past x 399 he moves no further. Resets walk_step to 6.

Steps the walking figure's animation: every seventh call the three sprites take the shapes listed at $90BA-$90BC, the middle sprite's alternating between its listed shape and the one it shows less one; on the other calls each sprite shows its shape less one. Each shape is turned to face walk_dir first (face_shape).
face_shape for the shape one below A.

Makes sure sprite shape A faces the way in walk_dir (1 left, $FF right), keeping A, X and Y. The way each shape faces is kept at $0400 plus the shape's low five bits, the top row of the text screen, which the bitmap covers; when it differs, the shape is mirrored where it lies (flip_shape, from flip_base $48: the shapes at $4800).

Turns the figure to face left unless facing is already 1, the value it writes: from $FF (right) and from 0 (standing or firing). Its three sprites take the shapes listed at $90BA, each turned to face walk_dir, and the animation restarts.
Turns the figure to face right unless facing is already $FF, the value it writes. Its three sprites take the shapes listed at $90BD, the third then $2E, and the animation restarts.

Raster handler of the stages, line 216: switches to the text screen for the status lines (VIC bank 0, text from the character set at $0800, screen $0400, black background, fine scroll from text_scroll), copies the shadow registers to the VIC (positions $0E3F-$0E4F to $D000-$D010, colours $0E51-$0E60 to $D020-$D02F, enable $0E50 to $D015, pointers $0E61-$0E68 to $47F8), keeps the sprite collisions in $1027, and flips $0E5F, sprite 7's colour, between 0 and 1 each frame so the sight flickers. In the ending it scrolls the ending text up a pixel every tenth frame and a line every eight pixels. Then plays the music (play_music) in the ending and the effects (play_effects) in a stage, unless a sample is playing. Next handler irq_top on line 1.

The ending's text: when a line has scrolled, rows 21-23 of the text screen move up a line and the next line of the ending text, thirty characters at (ending_ptr), is written on row 24. A line that starts with $FF is blank and one byte long. After 23 lines ending_running is cleared.

Raster handler of the stages, line 1: VIC bank 1 with the bitmap at $6000 and the screen at $4400, multicolour, $D011 from bitmap_d011, and the background dark grey in the shoot-out (stage 0) or white in the others, unless a picture is being drawn. Then moves points onto the score (count_score) and returns. Next handler irq_bottom on the line in bottom_line ($9086).
BIT $01A9: hides the LDA #$01 at $3B4D, where the other stages branch in, so the shoot-out (stage 0) gets $0B, dark grey, and the others 1, white
Pulls Y, X and A off the stack and returns from the interrupt: the end of every raster handler, as the KERNAL's own handler ends.

The BRK handler: saves A, X and Y, resets the CIAs and the interrupt vectors (the KERNAL's IOINIT and restore_vectors), the screen editor (CINT), and jumps to $C057. That address holds picture data in the game, so a BRK would crash it; the only BRK in the code is the check in check_shot.
Saves A, X and Y in zpa_0A, zpa_0B and zpa_0C.
Loads A, X and Y back from zpa_0A, zpa_0B and zpa_0C.
Writes 0 to the sound chip's registers $D400-$D416, silencing the three voices.
Copies the KERNAL's table of vectors ($FD30-$FD4F) back into $0314-$0333.

Moves points from pending ($8FA4-$8FA7) onto the score ($8FA8-$8FAB), both four BCD bytes, low first, in decimal mode: 1 a frame while fewer than 100 are waiting, $99 while 1000 or more, and between them $0B, which is not a BCD number. Taken from pending and added to the score in decimal mode, $0B leaves digits above 9 in the bytes, and the adds after it carry them on as extra points: a bonus of 594 puts 706 on the score, one of 1920 puts 2096 (live). Then writes the score's eight digits, without leading zeros, in yellow at (score_at) and into score_text ($8E41) and last_score_text ($8F51). Returns at once when nothing is pending.

Draws the shoot-out's status: bad_guys_killed as a bar of character $24 on row 22 from column 0, then a bar of $12 (twelve) $20 characters from column 27, overwritten by a bar of bad_guys_left in $24 (draw_bar).

Clears rows 16 to 23 of the text screen in green and writes the hall of fame: its two title lines ($8C48, $8C5E) in light blue and the five entries ($8C74, eleven characters each: three initials and eight digits).

Compares score_text with the five hall of fame entries, best first. When it beats one, moves that entry and the ones below it down a place (the fifth falls off), writes the score into the free place with three spaces for the initials, shows the table and takes the initials from the keyboard: letters A to Z and the space, three at most (a fourth starts again from the first), RETURN to finish, with a flashing cursor. Then waits and goes to the title.
Points zpa_26 at hall of fame entry zpa_0D ($8C74 + 11×zpa_0D) and zpa_28 at the one after it; also sets zpa_0E to zpa_0D.
"PRESS FIRE BUTTON", seventeen screen codes, written under the hall of fame
The first of the title's three credits lines, forty screen codes: "GRAPHICS: J.DARNELL N.BAIKALOFF J.PORCH"
A space after the graphics credit that nothing reads
Passes of the title's wait loop to the next count of $3E69
The title's credits line changes when this has counted 200 of $3E68's rounds
A byte between the credit counters that nothing reads
Which credits line the title shows: 3 the graphics credit, 2 the design credit, 1 Mastertronic's
A byte after credit_line that nothing reads, 10
The reset header start_stage copies to $8000: the cold and warm start vectors, both $0C00, and the letters CBM80 ($C3 $C2 $CD $38 $30) that make the KERNAL jump through them on a reset
Rounds of the hoofbeats' other pattern the caught train plays as it stops, from 10, before the bonus is counted

Runs the gunmen, every fifth call (gunmen_step) from the shoot-out's loop. Each of the four gunman sprites (3 to 6) that is showing a gunman is animated (gunman_step). One that is free counts down its own delay ($913A, reloaded from $9142) and then takes a hiding place: one of the sixteen, chosen at random from CIA 1's timer and the raster line, that has not had its gunman hit, trying up to 255 times (after that its delay is left at 0, so its next try is 256 steps away). The test for a place in use reads place_used at the gunman's number ($3ED4, LDA $914D,X) instead of the place's, so a gunman can take a place another gunman is in, and is turned away while place 0, 1, 2 or 3 (his own number) is taken. The sprite turns white, the place is marked in use ($914D), and the sprite goes to the place's position from place_x ($9169, whose bit 0 is the position's ninth bit) and place_y ($916A).
A place at random, 0 to 15: CIA 1's timer A, both bytes, and the raster line together
JMP $37E3, into check_shot's bonus: never runs, since it follows the JMP above it and nothing jumps here
Should test the chosen place, place_used,Y; tests place_used,X, X being the gunman's number
Leftover: a NOP, then an older build of gunman_step's first part, $3F3A-$3FFF, as DATA2 brought it, the same bytes as $8810-$88D5. Nothing runs or reads them
The base start indexes from to copy the three shapes ($3FFF+X, X from $C0 down to 1); the byte itself is the older build's last

Three sprite shapes, $4000-$40BF, the rider thrown from his horse: start copies them into the stack page ($0101-$01C0) before the game draws anything at $4000, and build_ride_screen puts them back at $7300 as shapes $CC-$CE on every ride. Once the game runs, $4000-$43FF is VIC bank 1's first kilobyte: the shapes 0 to 3 of the stages and a ride's text screen
In play, the sight's shape (sprite shape 0) from its sixteenth byte: start_play writes sight_shape here
In play, sprite shape 1: the arrow, or the first gunman's shape, drawn by gunman_step
In play, the arrow's rows in shape 1, written from arrow_frames
In play on the train, the screen's row 4: the engine is drawn in on the left from here, a row 40 bytes on at $40C8, $40F0, $4118 and $4140
Sixty-four zeros after the three shapes, the end of DATA2
the engine's second row on the train's screen
the engine's third row on the train's screen

DATA3's own reset header: cold and warm start vectors at $8010, where the older build begins, and CBM80; start_stage replaces it with cbm80_header before play. clear_obstacles clears $8001 and $8003, the vectors' high bytes
Seven bytes after DATA3's header that nothing reads

An older build of the game's code, $8010-$8727, as DATA3 brought it: the code from check_shot's end to gunmen_appear's ($37F3-$3EE6 today), assembled $4819 to $481D bytes higher. Nothing runs it: from the first ride on, $8010-$87DF is the rides' map buffer, five rows of 400 characters, and clear_map clears it to $880F
The older build from the middle of its count_score on
The older build's last forty bytes, zeros to $880E, and a stray $86 at $880F before gunman_step

Animates gunman X (0-3, sprite 3+X) in his hiding place, drawing into his sprite shape (1+X, at $4040+X×64) from the bottom row up. A hit gunman dissolves: each step clears random pixels of his shape until it is empty, and the place is freed (gunman_gone). Otherwise he comes out of the place over 5, 6 or 7 steps, by its kind ($916C): kinds 0 and 1 rise from below, 5 or 6 rows of $9116 or $911B drawn a row more each step; kind 2 slides in from the right (the eleven rows at $9121 shifted right less each step) and kind 3 from the left ($912C shifted left). The way is kept as a letter in gunman_way ($9148): $42 B, $52 R, $4C L; waits seven steps; fires once (effects bit 6 and gunman_fires); and goes back the way he came, after which the place is freed.
Frees gunman X's sprite and his hiding place, and reloads his delay from $9142.
Points Y at the last row of gunman X's sprite shape ($4040 + X×64 + $3E, its last byte but one) and loads X from zpa_04.

Mirrors sprite shape Y left to right where it lies: toggles its facing byte at $0400+Y, finds its address (flip_base×256 + Y×64, shape_address) and, row by row for its 21 rows, reverses the order of the three bytes and the bits of each byte (mirror_byte).
Mirrors the row at zpa_03 in the shape at (zpa_26): its three bytes in reverse order, each through mirror_byte; moves zpa_03 on three.

Mirrors a byte of a sprite: its eight bits in reverse order, through $90F6 (the high nibble) and $9106 (the low nibble). Right for the shoot-out's sprites and the horse's, which are not multicolour. The rider's two shapes ($CA, $CB) are multicolour and are mirrored too: there the two bits of each pixel swap as well, so colours 01 and 10 trade places, which does not show because both are white ($D025 and $D028 are 1 on a ride). $00 and $FF come back as they are.
Puts the address of shape A (counting from flip_base: A×64 + flip_base×256) in zpa_26 and zpa_27.
